Alex / Everwell team — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap + asks so we can kick off a proper dedicated-capacity pilot: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary workload: interactive clinical summarization + short-context retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) in sessions.
- Typical session: ~1-3 turns; average request ~250–300 tokens (streaming).
- Targets you called out: p95 latency ~150ms–200ms (end-to-end), p99 < 400ms acceptable for peaks.
- Throughput & concurrency: steady-state 100–150 req/s, occasional bursts to ~250 req/s, concurrent sessions ~50–70.

Outstanding asks from Redwood to size dedicated capacity
1) Can you share a sample load profile (token distribution, per-minute arrival pattern) — if you have a CSV that’s ideal.
2) Confirm model variants you expect to use in pilot (big model vs smaller fallbacks) and whether quantized variants are acceptable for inference.
3) Any hard budget or cost-per-token ceiling we should respect for recommendations?

What we propose next (internal + customer-visible)
- Redwood engineering will run a side-by-side GPU matrix (A100 80GB, H100 80GB, L4 equivalents where applicable) with mixed quantization configs against a synthetic load that mirrors your profile.
- Pilot acceptance: p95 latency within 1.25x of your target for streaming first-token and sustained throughput that meets steady-state expected throughput.
- Deliverable: bench matrix + recommended reserved slab (initial pilot sizing + scale runway) and a validation plan for a 2-week pilot.

Attachments: none yet — if you can drop the load profile CSV that helps.

Next steps
- Can you send the load CSV and confirm the model flavors?
- We’ll loop in Performance to produce the GPU shortlist and a pilot timeline.

Thanks — I’ll summarize back here once we have the CSV.

— Tessa

Confirmations / updates:
- The p95 target we had in mind is ~150ms end-to-end (client → model → first streaming token). p99 can be tolerated up to ~400ms for large-context requests.
- Steady-state throughput: ~120 req/s (this is what 95% of traffic looks like). Bursts happen up to ~250 req/s during peak windows (morning syncs).
- Average request size: ~250 tokens (we do have a long-tail to ~1k tokens for some aggregated summaries).
- Concurrency: 50–65 concurrent active sessions typically.
- Model plan for the pilot: we want to validate 2 variants — a 13B-cost-optimized model (quantized acceptable) and a higher-quality 34B variant (prefer float16 or 8-bit quantized only if quality checks pass).

Attachments included: everwell_load_profile_v1.csv, gpu_shortlist_matrix.xlsx (small internal matrix showing traffic slices).

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Tessa / Ben — read the thread and the CSV. Below is a concise test plan and an initial hardware recommendation to discuss before we present to Everwell: 

Proposed test matrix
- Models: 13B quantized (Q4/8), 34B f16 (and 34B Q8 if quality check passes).
- Hardware SKUs: H100-80GB, A100-80GB (PCIe if H100 not available), and L4 (or cloud inference instance with similar INT8 throughput).
- Workload: replay load_profile CSV to recreate minute-level arrival patterns; include sustained 120 req/s baseline and 250 req/s 5-minute bursts.
- Sequence lengths: 250 tokens (typical), 600 tokens (tail), 1k tokens (rare).
- Metrics: first-token latency (streaming), end-to-end p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec per GPU, NVLink/KV cache hit behavior; mem pressure and OOM events.

Acceptance criteria (aligned to customer)
- steady-state: first-token p95 <= 187ms; p99 <= 400ms for peak bursts.
- throughput: sustain >= 120 req/s with <=10% error/retry rate.

Pilot sizing recommendation (initial)
- For initial 2-week pilot (validate perf + quality): start with 4x H100-80GB as the baseline to run parallel model variants and have headroom for KV cache & burst replay.
- If cost sensitivity is critical we can run A100-80GB as a cheaper alternative but expect ~15–25% lower tokens/sec for the heavy 34B runs vs H100. L4 shows promise for the 13B quantized path but needs verification on long-tail token batches (1k).
- For a production reserved slab to meet steady-state + 30% buffer = targeting sustained 150 req/s, estimate: 6x H100-80GB (or equivalent) — we’ll produce exact numbers after bench runs.

Timeline
- Smoke test / microbench (internal): start Mon Sep 14 (2 days)
- Full benchmark matrix run: week of Sep 21 (3–5 days)
- Deliverable: bench report + recommended reserved slab and pilot runbook by Sep 27.

I’ll spin up the perf jobs once Ben confirms infra and I have access to the realistic sample tokens (CSV looks fine).

— Karthik
